title: Evaluate health programmes

blocks.heading: Evaluate health programmes
blocks.text: Primary health care links accessible care, prevention and community needs; hospitals, trained doctors and supporting workers provide complementary capabilities. Trained auxiliaries need suitable roles, supervision and referral support; immunisation, community programmes and safe-water provision address different needs. Compare accessible coverage, quality, staffing, maintenance and cost rather than simply counting buildings.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Follow the mechanism
blocks.text: A fictional health budget can expand a staffed mobile service or equip a fixed centre for more specialised care. Outreach can reduce journeys for routine needs; a fixed centre may handle cases needing equipment that cannot travel. Neither replaces an effective referral route. Priorities depend on the pattern of need, coverage and operating capacity, with benefits and limitations weighed for both choices.

blocks.heading: Programme evidence and limits
blocks.text: [WHO’s primary-health-care overview](https://www.who.int/health-topics/primary-health-care) describes community-centred services and broader health conditions. Its [2024 Namibia account](https://www.afro.who.int/news/namibia-reaches-key-milestone-eliminating-mother-child-transmission-hiv-and-hepatitis-b) reports integration of maternal-child and primary health services and progress on reducing vertical transmission. These show linked programmes, not proof that every household is served. Checked 20 October 2026; exact clinical procedures and schedules are outside this lesson.
